0.long_answer: CYP1A2 is a cytochrome P450 enzyme that plays a key role in the metabolism of xenobiotics, including toluene. It is one of the enzymes involved in transforming foreign compounds into metabolites that the body can more easily eliminate. Unlike some P450 enzymes such as CYP2E1—which is also important in toluene metabolism but is located on a different chromosome—CYP1A2 is encoded by a gene on chromosome 15. This gene location is a distinguishing feature that, along with its metabolic activities in the liver, makes CYP1A2 particularly significant in both drug metabolism and the processing of environmental chemicals.
